text: After all this, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, there came Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,

versions.text: After all this, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra came up — son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew of v.1 has no verb; the main clause is completed in v.6 ("This Ezra came up from Babylon"). Supplying "came up" here anticipates and duplicates v.6, and the em dash before the genealogy reads awkwardly aloud. A lighter supplied verb keeps the flow without the repetition.

text: son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and because the hand of the LORD his God was upon him, the king granted him everything he asked.
Some of the Israelites, along with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of that seventh year of the king.
He had set out from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he came to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the good hand of his God was upon him.
For Ezra had set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to do it, and to teach its statutes and judgments in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe, a scholar in matters concerning the commandments and statutes of the LORD for Israel:
Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
I hereby decree that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who freely choose to go up to Jerusalem, may go with you.
For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which is in your hand,
and to bring the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
together with all the silver and gold you may obtain throughout the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings of the people and the priests for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
Therefore with this money you are to buy without delay bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.

versions.text: With this money you are to buy bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
versions.explanation: The Aramaic includes both the connective "therefore" (kol-qobel denah) and the adverb asparna ("diligently, without delay"), which the translation renders elsewhere (vv. 21, 26) but omits here.

text: Whatever seems best to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do it according to the will of your God.
And the vessels entrusted to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver them before the God of Jerusalem.
Whatever else is needed for the house of your God, whatever you must provide, pay for it from the royal treasury.

I, King Artaxerxes, further decree to all the treasurers of the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, asks of you, it shall be done with all diligence —
up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.
Whatever the God of heaven has commanded, let it be done with care for the house of the God of heaven, so that no wrath may come upon the realm of the king and his sons.
Be it also known to you that no tax, tribute, or toll may be imposed on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River — all who know the laws of your God; and teach those who do not know them.
And whoever will not obey the Law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with all diligence: death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who put it into the king's heart to glorify the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,

and who extended his steadfast love to me before the king, his counselors, and all the king's mighty officials. And I took courage, for the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
